HubFAQ.blA1: On LassTreffen.at you will find current {categoryNoun} {whereWith} — from big concerts and festivals to neighbourhood fairs, markets and club nights. The overview is updated several times a day.
HubFAQ.blQ2: How do I find {categoryNoun} {whereWith} on a map?
HubFAQ.blA2: Every event is located on the interactive map at /en/map. There you can filter events by location, category and date range — ideal for seeing what is happening right around you.
HubFAQ.blQ3: Where do the {categoryNoun} for {where} come from?
HubFAQ.blA3: The listings are aggregated from official ticket vendors (Eventim, oeticket), the state's tourism portals, municipal calendars and event aggregators. Duplicates are filtered out automatically.
HubFAQ.blQ4: Is the event overview for {where} free to use?
HubFAQ.blA4: Yes, browsing and filtering is completely free and works without signing up. If you want to save events, invite friends or follow artists, you can optionally create a free account.
HubFAQ.thQ1: How many {heroNoun} are there in Austria right now?
HubFAQ.thA1: LassTreffen.at currently lists {nice} events in the {category} category across Austria. The database is updated daily from official ticket vendors, municipal calendars and tourism portals.
HubFAQ.thQ2: Where can I find {heroNoun} near me?
HubFAQ.thA2: On the interactive map at /en/map you can filter all {categoryLower} events by location. In addition, every state has its own overview page (e.g. /en/wien/{slug}, /en/steiermark/{slug}) with a local focus.
HubFAQ.thA3: Yes, the entire event search is free and accessible without registration. Ticket prices — where provided by the organiser — are shown directly on the event detail page; purchase and processing happen with the respective ticket vendor.
HubFAQ.thQ4: How up to date is the event list for {theme}?
HubFAQ.thA4: The {theme} events are re-imported several times a day from more than 140 sources. Cancelled or postponed dates are detected automatically and flagged accordingly.
HubFAQ.thQ5: Can I submit my own {theme} events as an organiser?
HubFAQ.thA5: Yes — you can suggest your own events via the submission form. Submissions are moderated and published once they meet the quality bar.
HubFAQ.gemQ1: What events are on in {gemeinde} today?
HubFAQ.gemA1: LassTreffen.at currently lists {nice} events within 10 km of {gemeinde} ({plz}, {bundesland}). The list ranges from village fairs and markets to concerts, sports events and cultural programmes — updated daily from official sources.
HubFAQ.gemQ2: How are the events for {gemeinde} collected?
HubFAQ.gemA2: The listings come from municipal calendars ({gemeinde} and neighbouring places), the tourism portals of {bundesland}, ticket vendors and regional event feeds. Duplicates are merged automatically so you never read the same announcement twice.
HubFAQ.gemQ3: Are events from municipalities near {gemeinde} included?
HubFAQ.gemA3: Yes — the 10 km radius around {gemeinde} automatically covers events in neighbouring places. A list of the closest places with their own event overview is further down this page.
HubFAQ.gemQ4: Can I submit an event in {gemeinde} myself?
HubFAQ.gemA4: Yes. Clubs, organisers and private individuals can submit their own dates through the submission form. Entries are moderated and listed publicly if they meet the quality bar — usually within 24 hours.
HubFAQ.gemActQ1: What is there to do in and around {gemeinde}?
HubFAQ.gemActA1: LassTreffen.at currently lists {nice} things to do and attractions around {gemeinde} ({plz}, {bundesland}) — from pools, museums and castles to hiking, cycling and family destinations. Every activity has its own page with opening hours, a map and directions.
HubFAQ.gemActQ2: Where do the attractions for {gemeinde} come from?
HubFAQ.gemActA2: The entries come from the regions' official tourism databases (Feratel Deskline), which the local tourism boards in {bundesland} also maintain. Permanently closed businesses are detected and removed from the lists automatically.
HubFAQ.gemActQ3: Are the things to do around {gemeinde} suitable in the rain?
HubFAQ.gemActA3: Many of the listed destinations are indoor activities such as indoor pools, thermal baths, museums or climbing halls. Each detail page states whether an activity is indoor, outdoor or mixed, so you can plan around the weather.
HubFAQ.gemActQ4: What is the admission price for attractions around {gemeinde}?
HubFAQ.gemActA4: Where operators publish prices, LassTreffen.at shows a price note directly on the activity page. Many destinations such as hiking trails, natural monuments or playgrounds are free; binding prices always come from the operator.

burgenland.lead: Between Lake Neusiedl, rolling vineyards and the Pannonian plain, Burgenland has an event scene that goes far beyond tourism clichés.
burgenland.body: The season starts earlier here than in the rest of Austria. From April onwards, the neighbourhoods around Rust, Mörbisch and Podersdorf switch into event mode — from lakeside opera festivals and wine tastings along the Lake Neusiedl cycling route to church fairs in practically every village. In summer there is hardly a weekend without a wine-tavern festival or open-air concert; in winter, Christmas markets in Eisenstadt and the Esterhazy Palace concert season take over. Burgenland is also Austria's festival backyard: Lovely Days, Nova Rock and the Pannonia Fields deliver three weeks of music tourism around Nickelsdorf every year.
burgenland.tips: If you are after authentic local tradition, look out for St Martin's celebrations and harvest church fairs in Oberpullendorf and Oberwart in autumn — that is where things happen away from the main tourist routes.

wien.lead: Vienna is Austria's event capital, and not just because of its size — it is the density of subcultures you will not find anywhere else in the country.
wien.body: Between a Philharmonic concert at the Musikverein and a techno night at Grelle Forelle or Flex lie all of ten metro stops. Vienna runs in parallel: an international classical scene (Musikverein, Konzerthaus, State Opera), a club and rave scene with Resident Advisor reach (Flex, Fluc, Volksgarten, Pratersauna, Werk), more than 200 theatre and cabaret stages, and one of the largest Christmas-market clusters in Europe. Add the student scene around WU, TU, the University of Vienna and BOKU, open-air events in the Prater and on the Danube Island, and a ball season from November to carnival that is unmatched in Austria.
wien.tips: For the densest club programme, try Thursdays — many Viennese labels use the start of the week for resident nights with cheaper entry and better chances at the door.

niederoesterreich.lead: Lower Austria is the largest state in Austria by area — and its event landscape is just as spread out.
niederoesterreich.body: Between Krems on the Danube, the Weinviertel, the Wachau and the Industrieviertel in the south lie entire worlds. The Wachau revolves around wine festivals (the apricot fair in Spitz, the wine harvest festival in Retz), classical music (Grafenegg, Schallaburg) and boat events on the Danube. The Weinviertel has Austria's densest network of church fairs — almost every weekend there is a village festival with brass music somewhere. The Industrieviertel around Wiener Neustadt and Baden brings larger concert halls and musical productions. Lower Austria has no metropolis of its own, but many small and mid-sized towns with their own cultural pulse: Krems, St. Pölten, Klosterneuburg, Wiener Neustadt, Amstetten.
niederoesterreich.tips: Wachau summer: the apricot festival in Spitz, the open-air Danube cinema in Krems, and the Grafenegg classical season. In late summer all three overlap — book tickets six or more weeks ahead.

oberoesterreich.lead: Upper Austria swings between urban Linz, the alpine Salzkammergut and the industrial axis of Wels, Steyr and Enns — with an event spectrum to match.
oberoesterreich.body: With Ars Electronica, Linz hosts one of the world's most important digital-art festivals, anchored culturally by the Lentos museum. The club scene around Posthof, Stadtwerkstatt and KAPU plays several nights a week. In the Salzkammergut, lake festivals on the Traunsee, Attersee and Lake Hallstatt dominate, alongside the Narcissus Festival in Bad Aussee and the Salzburg Festival spillover in Bad Ischl. Steyr and Wels regularly host trade fairs and concerts in smaller halls. And Linz is the central hub for the student scene of the JKU and the University of Arts, with the nightlife to go with it.
oberoesterreich.tips: Ars Electronica (usually early September) takes over the whole city for a week — if you want to stay overnight in Linz, book three or more months ahead.

salzburg.lead: Culturally, Salzburg is split in two: the festival city in summer, and the alpine event region around Zell am See, Saalbach and the Pinzgau for the rest of the year.
salzburg.body: The Salzburg Festival (late July to late August) is the international flagship — six weeks of opera, drama and concerts that turn the city upside down. Outside of that, Salzburg runs as a classic tourism destination: Mozart concerts almost daily, Krampus runs in Advent, Rauhnächte traditions in Werfen and the Lungau. In parallel, the Gastein valley and the area around Zell am See-Kaprun are event hubs for ski tourism in winter and trail-running events in summer. ARGEkultur and the Rockhouse in the city of Salzburg keep the indie and concert scene going all year round.
salzburg.tips: For festival lovers on a budget: the Siemens Festival Nights screen selected productions for free on Kapitelplatz. No reservation, no entry fee — seats start filling up from around 7 pm.

steiermark.lead: Styria bundles three very different event regions into one state: Graz, the Ausseerland-Salzkammergut and the Styrian wine road.
steiermark.body: Graz, European Capital of Culture in 2003, has cultivated that legacy to this day — the Kunsthaus, Schauspielhaus and the opera carry the core scene, while the Murinsel summer and the Styriarte fill the warm months with festival programming. Postgarage, PPC and Orpheum Extra are the established indie and club venues. In the Ausseerland, the Narcissus Festival, church fairs and pilgrimages overlap with alpine tourism. The Styrian wine road around Gamlitz and Leutschach lives off wine-tavern festivals, tastings and harvest celebrations. On top of that: Aflenz Splashline, the Nova Rock neighbourhood, and the Graz student scene with the University of Graz, Med Uni and the University of Arts.
steiermark.tips: Styriarte tickets (late June to mid-July, early music) typically sell out in March/April — spontaneous visitors often have better luck with the side-row seats at the palace concerts.

kaernten.lead: Carinthia is Austria's lake state — and the event season revolves accordingly around Lake Wörthersee, Lake Millstatt, Lake Weissensee and Lake Ossiach.
kaernten.body: The Wörthersee has hosted the bigger open-air concerts and beach parties for decades, and Klagenfurt's Wörthersee stadium doubles as a venue for stadium acts. In the shoulder season the focus shifts to Nassfeld, Bad Kleinkirchheim and the ski resorts, where après-ski events and season openings fill the calendars. Klagenfurt itself has solid concert venues in the Volkertheater, the Stadthaus and the Wörthersee-Saal; the scene around Kulturverein Kramer and the Villach city theatre regularly delivers indie culture. Typically Carinthian: the Kufenstechen, church fairs and pilgrimages that keep folk tradition alive in the side valleys.
kaernten.tips: Wörthersee classical concerts mostly take place in July and are often under-booked — the box office is more of a real option here than elsewhere in Austria.

tirol.lead: Tyrol is the state with the clearest event seasonality — winter ski events and summer mountain events shape the calendar.
tirol.body: Innsbruck forms the urban centre, with Treibhaus, the Weekender club, Bäckerei and the P.M.K. cultural centre as the scene's venues. The ski openings in Ischgl, Sölden, St. Anton and Obergurgl draw an international après-ski crowd in November and December. In summer, the centre of gravity shifts to the Zillertal (the Zellberg Buam alpine party, the Gauderfest in Zell am Ziller), the Ötztal (trail running, mountain-bike events) and the Pitztal. The Tyrolean Festival Erl (near Kufstein) brings ambitious opera in summer. The carnival mask processions — such as the Telfs Schleicherlauf — are internationally recognised as UNESCO intangible cultural heritage.
tirol.tips: For genuine Tyrolean tradition, look at the carnival runs of Telfs, Imst and Rottenburg — they only take place every three to five years and draw tens of thousands.

vorarlberg.lead: Vorarlberg is small but dense: Lake Constance to the west, the Arlberg to the east, and in between a scene built around the Bregenz festival stage in summer and ski tourism in winter.
vorarlberg.body: The Bregenz Festival (July/August) on the floating lake stage is part of music theatre's world heritage — it is the flagship that puts Bregenz on the event map far beyond Austria. Dornbirn and Feldkirch add their own smaller subscenes with the Poolbar Festival, the Conrad Sohm club and the Spielboden. The Arlberg (Lech, Zürs, St. Anton — the latter borders Tyrol) is Austria's most exclusive ski region with its own event calendar from ski openings to Tanzcafé Arlberg. In the Montafon, the Bregenzerwald and the Walgau, traditional customs such as bonfire nights and the ceremonial cattle drives live on.
vorarlberg.tips: The Poolbar Festival in Feldkirch (July, Alte Bürgermühle) is one of the most lovable mid-sized culture spots in western Austria — combining club acts, literature and exhibitions.

musik.title: Concerts, Festivals & Live Music in Austria
musik.seoTitle: Concerts & Festivals 2026 — Live Music in Austria
musik.description: All concerts, festivals and live music events in Austria at a glance. Rock, pop, classical, electronic — updated daily for every state.
musik.heroText: From festival weekends to living-room concerts — Austria's music agenda in one place.
musik.bodyIntro: Austria has a dense music scene: from the Frequency Festival and Nova Rock to the Vienna State Opera and wine-tavern concerts in Burgenland. LassTreffen.at aggregates daily from official ticket vendors, venue calendars and regional event portals so you never miss a show.

kultur.title: Culture & Stage — Theatre, Art, Cabaret
kultur.description: Theatre premieres, cabaret nights, art exhibitions and stage events across Austria. A culture calendar updated daily.
kultur.heroText: Stage, screen, gallery — culture in Austria, updated daily.
kultur.bodyIntro: From Burgtheater premieres in Vienna and Capital-of-Culture projects in Graz to regional cabaret in Bregenz: Austria's cultural landscape is dense, regional and usually sold out. LassTreffen.at collects theatre, readings, vernissages and cabaret in one place.

nightlife.title: Nightlife & Party — Clubs, DJ Sets, After-Shows
nightlife.seoTitle: Clubs, Parties & DJ Sets in Austria
nightlife.description: Club nights, DJ sets, open-air raves and parties in Vienna, Graz, Innsbruck, Salzburg and the rest of Austria. Always up to date.
nightlife.heroText: Until the lights come on — and a little longer.
nightlife.bodyIntro: Austrian nightlife stretches from Vienna's Flex and Graz's Postgarage to Burgenland's summer open-airs and Innsbruck's après-ski clubs. We aggregate club line-ups, festival closings and pop-up events so you don't find out about a gig only after it happened.

kulinarik.title: Food & Drink — Wine Taverns, Wine Festivals, Food Events
kulinarik.seoTitle: Wine Festivals, Taverns & Food Events in Austria
kulinarik.description: Wine taverns, tastings, street-food markets, brewery tours and culinary weekends in every Austrian state.
kulinarik.heroText: Wine from the winemaker, beer from the brewery, food trucks on the market square.
kulinarik.bodyIntro: Austria's culinary calendar is denser than its wine cellar: Burgenland wine tastings, Styria's pumpkin-festival autumn, Naschmarkt events in Vienna and brewery tours in Tyrol. LassTreffen.at bundles food and drink dates from all nine states.

maerkte.title: Markets & Festivals — Flea Markets, Village Fairs, Advent Markets
maerkte.seoTitle: Markets, Fairs & Kirtag Festivals in Austria
maerkte.description: Flea markets, farmers' markets, advent markets, village fairs and church fairs — Austria's tradition agenda at a glance.
maerkte.heroText: Where Austria gets together — with punch, beer and roast pork.
maerkte.bodyIntro: From Vienna's Christmas markets and the Urfahraner Markt in Linz to village church fairs in remote Styrian and Burgenland municipalities: markets and fairs are Austria's densest event type. We scrape official municipal and tourism calendars so even the small festivals become visible.

sport.title: Sport & Movement — Runs, Matches, Tournaments
sport.seoTitle: Running Events, Football Matches & Sport in Austria
sport.description: Fun runs, home football matches, marathons, Ski World Cup races and amateur tournaments in every state. An up-to-date sport calendar.
sport.heroText: Pick up your bib, put on the jersey, go.
sport.bodyIntro: From a Rapid home game and the Wings for Life run to Styrian Ski World Cup races and amateur competitions: Austria's sport calendar thrives on the mix of professional events and club sport. LassTreffen.at aggregates both — from the Bundesliga to the village fun run.

natur.title: Nature & Adventure — Hiking, Climbing, Outdoors
natur.seoTitle: Hikes, Outdoor Events & Nature in Austria
natur.description: Guided hikes, climbing tours, cycling marathons, nature experiences and outdoor events in every Austrian state.
natur.heroText: Alpine views, the open expanse of Lake Neusiedl, the Danube floodplains — things are happening outside.
natur.bodyIntro: Austria's nature calendar ranges from the Hohe Tauern and the Grossglockner Trail to the Wachau cycling routes and the Lake Neusiedl National Park. LassTreffen.at lists guided tours, nature-park events and outdoor workshops from all nine states — including the small club hikes.

bildung.title: Knowledge & Career — Talks, Workshops, Fairs
bildung.seoTitle: Talks, Workshops & Career Events in Austria
bildung.description: Lectures, training workshops, career fairs, startup events and university dates across Austria.
bildung.heroText: From course to congress to trade fair — input for your brain.
bildung.bodyIntro: Austria's knowledge landscape spans the University of Vienna and TU Graz as well as regional university-of-applied-sciences campuses and private training providers. LassTreffen.at aggregates lecture series, career fairs, startup meetups and university events — including the publicly accessible dates of all Austrian universities.

familie.title: Family & Kids — Events With and For Children
familie.description: Children's theatre, family festivals, holiday workshops, climbing parks and weekend activities for families in every state.
familie.heroText: For kids who want to experience something and parents who have to plan it.
familie.bodyIntro: From the Musikverein children's series in Vienna and children's theatre at Schönbrunn to knights' days at castles and adventure farms in the Salzkammergut: LassTreffen.at collects family events from all states — updated daily from official sources, so even spontaneous weekend planning works out.

community.title: Community & Leisure — Meetups, Clubs, Regulars' Tables
community.seoTitle: Meetups, Regulars' Tables & Community Events Austria
community.description: Language exchanges, meetups, club nights, leisure groups and community events in Vienna, Graz, Linz, Salzburg and across Austria.
community.heroText: Meet new people, revive old hobbies.
community.bodyIntro: Austria's community scene is growing: from Vienna's language cafés and board-game meetups in Graz to startup regulars' tables in Linz. LassTreffen.at pulls together Meetup, Eventbrite and club feeds so you don't have to click through ten apps to find out when the next community event near you takes place.

wellness.title: Wellness & Spirituality — Yoga, Meditation, Retreats
wellness.description: Yoga retreats, meditation sessions, thermal-spa events, wellness weekends and spiritual gatherings across Austria.
wellness.heroText: Take a breath, come to rest, tune in.
wellness.bodyIntro: Austria's thermal spas, yoga studios, meditation centres and spiritual retreats add up to an event canon of their own. LassTreffen.at aggregates spa weekend events, yoga workshops, mindfulness retreats and church gatherings from all nine states.

GemeindeHub.seoSourcesEvents: The event list is aggregated automatically from official municipal calendars, tourism portals, ticket vendors and event aggregators, and de-duplicated so you never read the same announcement twice.
